evidence: No supplier/test evidence in repository
implication: Attach component datasheet and conditions or qualify/remove
notes: "Up to 100,000 hours" removed sitewide. Fact check (research/technical-fact-base.md §2, §11.3): such figures are L70 LED lumen-maintenance points under LM-80/TM-21, not sign life; DOE flags 100,000-hour defaults as historically unsupported; power supplies fail first. Now: "long-life LEDs" plus an explanation of what an L70 rating means. Restore a number only with the LM-80 report and TM-21 projection for the LED used.

claim: Up to 80% less power than traditional glass neon
evidence: No methodology/baseline/source registered
implication: Supply dated source and comparison basis or remove
notes: "Up to 80% less power" removed. Fact check (§1C, §11.4): 57-85% less only against old magnetic-transformer neon; from ~5% more to 60% less against electronic-transformer neon; W/ft ignores brightness. Restore only with plug-measured watts and a like-for-like baseline.

evidence: Product copy only; no system-level certification/test record supplied
implication: Confirm whether components or full assembly are rated; publish installation limits
notes: IP67 now stated at component level only ("IP67-rated LED modules" in channel letters); neon/acrylic/lightbox pages say "outdoor build available". Fact check (§3, §11.5): IP67 is brief immersion, usually rated on the strip not the sign; US outdoor signs use UL wet-location marking; outdoor plug-in signs need GFCI. Restore a sign-level rating only with an assembled-sign test report.

evidence: Construction description; no test/datasheet register

Now "no glass tubes", "no gas or mercury", plus practical safety advice (mount out of reach, keep the power supply dry and ventilated).
